messages.author: 635bd93e270bc751
messages.subject: adding group variables to tps data
parts:
My first post.  Having used ImageJ and MorphoJ, I'm now looking to geomorph for one or two things, particularly graphics, which it seems to do better.  But I've already fallen at the first hurdle: reading in tps data and applying group variables to it. I'm sure I'm doing something really stupid, but can't find a way through even by looking through this forum (though Virginia Chu had a similar question last year).

Here's an Rmd document to explain the issue, together with a reduced dataset and a csv list of classifiers.  All ideas gratefully received.  Please show forbearance!

Nigel

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] adding group variables to tps data
parts:
Nigel,

for reading in the tps, please try installing from github, maybe the issue is the geomorph version you are using, because I can read you data fine here. For this, you need to install devtools and then run:

devtools::install_github(“geomorphR/geomorph”,ref = “Stable”)

To read in the csv file with the group data, you just need:

 classifier <- read.csv("classifier.csv")

Again, works fine for me. Just make sure the specimens in the csv file are in the same order as the shape data in the tps, and you are good to go.

Hope this helps

Antigoni

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Re: adding group variables to tps data
parts:
Nigel,

I am not sure where you expect your classifiers to appear, but when you read them in through the csv file, they become a separate object, that if in the same order as your tps specimens can be used for analyses. Whether R reads in loc as a factor or not is not particularly relevant here, but in any case if you want it to be a factor you can do something like classifier$loc <- as.factor(classifier$loc).

But maybe I am not understanding you correctly. At any rate, this sounds more like a basic R issue than a geomorph one, so maybe you should consider building some more general R knowledge? Plenty of online resources exist for that.

All the best,

Antigoni

Thanks, Antigoni, I accept the rebuke in your last paragraph. 

My concern was that my data failed to correspond to 3.4 of  Emma’s Quick Guide to geomorph 3.0.5.  When you’re following through the examples in a basic manual you tend (or at least I do) to worry if you don’t produce comparable outcomes. Which I thought made it ever-so-slightly a geomorph issue.

You were, of course, quite right. My tps data and the classifiers are now happily linked up, as you said they would be, and I am using them in analyses. So I can move on. 

Thank you for your advice.

Best wishes,

Nigel
